title: Speed up CI by running independent steps in parallel
summary: Most CI jobs run as one long serial script even when half the work doesn't depend on the other half. You can run independent steps in parallel for faster CI. We'll compare two ways to do it: shell backgrounding and Depot CI's parallel steps.
body_markdown: Performance came out roughly the same in my test: about 2m 30s for both, down from 2m 54s baseline. The difference is readability. Shell backgrounding turns one of your workflow steps into a mini process manager with shell functions, background PIDs,` wait` calls, and exit-status bookkeeping. Depot CI's` parallel:` block makes concurrency a first-class part of the workflow syntax, so reviewers and your future self can see the structure without parsing a shell script.
